title: amagilabs/amagi-draftbench
summary: Sweeps draft models and n-gram lookup for llama.cpp and vLLM, reporting tok/s, acceptance rate and peak VRAM per budget. Maps closely onto the seed's goal of picking a tiny draft for a 7B model on one GPU.

title: amanzainal/specdecode-roi
summary: Benchmarks whether speculative decoding pays off on your own model and GPU by sweeping draft length and finding break-even. Supports llama.cpp, so it could serve as the measurement harness for the 4090 experiment.

title: RanganBorah/SpecDecode
summary: Pairs a small draft with a larger target via llama.cpp on a laptop GPU, with benchmarks and a fine-tuned draft. The closest existing example of the seed's exact setup; the fine-tuned draft is an extra step to skip at first.

title: kuotunyu/qwen38-speculative-decoding-benchmark
summary: Pinned llama.cpp benchmark on a single RTX 4090 (WSL2) for Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M with MTP and n-gram speculation, using a paired-median and acceptance-rate methodology. Same GPU and runtime as the seed, but the draft is not a tiny model.

title: DRSY/SpeculativeDecoding
summary: A PyTorch and Hugging Face implementation comparing standard autoregressive decoding with speculative decoding. A simple baseline for checking correctness and speedup before porting to llama.cpp.

title: neerajdad123-byte/zero-vram-spec
summary: Shows speculative decoding for local GGUF code models in llama.cpp on an RTX 4050 with no draft model and no extra VRAM. A cheap baseline to compare the tiny-draft approach against on the same stack.

title: A Practical Investigation of Training-free Relaxed Speculative Decoding
summary: Practically tests training-free relaxed speculative decoding, which relaxes acceptance to gain speed without retraining. Directly matches the 'no retraining' constraint, but it trades away the lossless guarantee the seed implicitly wants.

title: A Sparse Glimpse of the Whole: Train-Free Self-Speculative Decoding
summary: Gives a unified speedup model showing that longer speculation can hurt when acceptance falls below relative drafting cost, and proposes a train-free self-speculative method. The cost model is useful for picking draft length on a 4090.

title: suryavanshi/speculative_decoding
summary: A basic PyTorch implementation of speculative decoding. Useful for understanding the accept/reject loop before moving to llama.cpp.

title: coffeegrind123/instantcoffee
summary: Docker Compose setup running llama.cpp with MTP and n-gram speculation for Qwen3.8-27B on one RTX 4090; useful as a reproducible llama.cpp configuration reference, not a tiny-draft result.

title: Approximate Speculative Decoding
summary: Approximate speculative decoding reuses target-scored suffixes after mismatches. It changes the output, so it departs from the lossless behavior the seed implies.

title: Speculative Acceptance Does Not Decay with Position: A Full-Length Diagnostic on Long Chain-of-Thought with Independent Drafts
summary: Measures acceptance rate versus generation position on long chain-of-thought with independent drafts; useful for checking whether acceptance holds over long 7B generations on the 4090.

title: GHGuide/self-draft
summary: Wraps MTP self-speculative decoding in llama.cpp with one flag, reporting ~1.5x on Arm64 cloud. Depends on MTP heads in the model and is not a tiny draft model; the hardware differs from the 4090.

title: bassrehab/speculative-decoding
summary: Reference implementation covering speculative decoding, EAGLE, Medusa and KV-cache compression, with roofline analysis. Helpful for reading the throughput model, though it is broader than the seed needs.

title: rajivmehtaflex/llama-server-up
summary: Automatically picks a speculative drafter and sizes llama-server to host RAM, but on CPU. Its drafter-selection logic is reusable for a GPU setup.

title: DLoop: Looped Speculative Decoding
summary: Proposes adaptive draft length so the target skips verification when it accepts every drafted token. Useful as a later tuning idea, but it assumes a looped draft/target design rather than a plain tiny draft model.

title: wtlow003/ngram-decoding
summary: Re-implements Prompt Lookup Decoding, a draft-free baseline that copies n-grams from the prompt; useful as a no-draft comparison point for the 7B run, not as the tiny-draft method.

title: joelvarun/suffixspec
summary: Draft-free suffix-retrieval speculation with confidence-tiered draft length; reduces wasted verification versus fixed prompt lookup but uses no draft model.

title: my-other-github-account/minimax-m27-ngram-spec-spark
summary: Reproducer for n-gram speculation in llama.cpp (--spec-type ngram-simple) on DGX Spark, showing 1.255x over autoregressive on a large MoE-class model; hardware and model differ from the seed.

title: joanmedina/qwen3-llama-cpp-inference-tuning
summary: Tuning guide and benchmarks for MTP and n-gram speculation in llama.cpp on AMD Strix Halo with Vulkan; reports +73% tok/s but on different hardware and model families.

title: Understanding Target Probability Reuse in Speculative Decoding
summary: Studies reuse of target next-token distributions when verifying draft trees. Relevant only if the project moves to tree drafting later.

title: Testing Processor Contracts in Speculative Decoding Engines
summary: Shows that speculative sampling preserves the target distribution only if logits processors get the right prefix and state; relevant only if the seed adds custom samplers, and it tests on tiny random models.

title: Speculative Speculative Decoding
summary: Parallelizes speculation with verification to remove the sequential dependency; a systems-level change that would need a custom engine rather than stock llama.cpp.

title: Speculative Diffusion is a Tale of Two Tradeoffs
summary: Analyzes speculative decoding against diffusion LLMs, which trade quality for speed. Only tangential to a lossless tiny-draft setup for a 7B model on a 4090.

title: CAST: Cost-Aware Speculative Trees from One-Pass Block Drafters
summary: Builds cost-aware verification trees from one-pass block drafters. Assumes a block drafter, not a plain tiny autoregressive draft.

title: naver-ai/DLoop
summary: Official PyTorch code for DLoop's looped drafting. Not directly usable for a plain tiny draft on a 7B model.

title: LongSpark: Efficient speculative decoding with a fixed-cost parallel drafter
summary: A fixed-cost parallel drafter aimed at long contexts. Likely needs a trained drafter, and the seed's short prompts are not its target.

title: Long-Context Drafting Does Not Require Long-Context Drafters
summary: Argues that long-context speculative drafting is not needed at ultra-long context. Mainly relevant to long prompts, which the seed does not target.

title: JetSpec++: Foresight Parallel Drafting with Self Refinements
summary: Co-designs a learned draft with self-refinement to hide draft cost; needs training a draft model, which conflicts with the seed's no-retraining constraint.

title: Phase-Scoped Query Layouts for Reference-Constrained Speculative Decoding
summary: Graph-level attention transformation for speculative verification on a quantized target, tested on CUDA; relevant only if the seed moves to a custom engine instead of llama.cpp.

title: Introducing Beam: Reflection’s 501B open-weight model
summary: Beam is a 501B-parameter sparse Mixture-of-Experts model (23B active) trained with 23.8T pretraining tokens and over 100M RL rollouts for coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads.
